Interface ExecutionSpec<S extends ExecutionSpec<S>>

Type Parameters:
S - The type that continues the declaration: the route, the group or the filter
All Known Subinterfaces:
FilterSpec<S>, HttpBodyRouteSpec<B>, HttpRouteGroup, HttpRouteSpec, LocatedBodyFilterSpec<T,B>, LocatedFilterSpec<T>, LocatedHttpBodyRouteSpec<T,B>, LocatedHttpRouteGroup<T>, LocatedHttpRouteSpec<T>, RouteSpec<S>
public sealed interface ExecutionSpec<S extends ExecutionSpec<S>> permits RouteSpec<S>, FilterSpec<S>
Where code runs: the handler of a route, see HttpRouteSpec, the handlers of the routes of a group, see HttpRouteGroup, or a filter, see FilterSpec. Every kind of code chooses its thread with the same methods, declared once here: a way to choose a thread that is added to this interface, e.g. a future executeOnIO(), is available to the routes, the groups and the filters at once.

On a route, the choice is the one of the route, like @ExecuteOn or @NonBlocking on a controller method. On a group, it is the default of the routes declared in the lambda of the group, and of its nested groups, wherever it is declared in the lambda: a route that chooses its thread, or a nested group that does, overrides it. On a filter, it is the choice of that filter only, like @ExecuteOn on a filter method. The last of executeOn and nonBlocking called wins.

routes.path("/reports", reports -> {
    reports.executeOn(TaskExecutors.BLOCKING);
    reports.before(request -> audit.record(request)).executeOn(TaskExecutors.IO);
    reports.GET("/{id}", (request, pathVariables) -> HttpResponse.ok(repository.find(pathVariables.getLong("id"))));
    reports.GET("/count").nonBlocking().handle((request, pathVariables) -> HttpResponse.ok(cache.count()));
});

  • Method Details

    • executeOn

      S executeOn(String executorName)
      Run the code on the named executor, like @ExecuteOn. It applies whatever the thread selection of the server.

      On a route, the handler runs on the executor, like @ExecuteOn on a controller method. On a group, the routes of the group, and of its nested groups, run on it, like @ExecuteOn on a controller, unless they, or a nested group, choose their thread. The media types and the executor of a group apply to its routes to handlers, including the implicit HEAD routes, the routes declared for several methods and the declared routes, and to the routes its locator routes locate, unless they, or a group of their LocatedRoutes, choose their own; not to its error and status routes.

      On a filter, the filter runs on the executor, like a filter method annotated @ExecuteOn: use it for a filter that blocks, e.g. on a database. The filter chain continues on that executor. An asynchronous filter is called on the executor, and the filter chain continues where its stage completes.

      Parameters:
      executorName - The name of the executor, e.g. TaskExecutors.BLOCKING
      Returns:
      The route, the group or the filter

    • nonBlocking

      S nonBlocking()
      Run the code without switching the thread. On a route, the handler runs on the event loop, like @NonBlocking on a controller method, when the server selects threads automatically: the route must not block. On a group, the default of its routes, like executeOn(String). On a filter, the default: the filter runs on the thread of the filter chain, like a filter method without @ExecuteOn.
      Returns:
      The route, the group or the filter
